title: Food and mood
titleChinese: 吃什么会影响你的情绪
paragraphs: Consuming food can be a pleasurable thing - we enjoy feasting on the mix of tastes and textures and it stops us feeling hungry too. Of course, food also gives us energy and the vitamins and minerals that our body needs. It‘s no wonder we spend so much time preparing and eating food. But what many of us don’t consider is how our emotions are affected by what we put into our bellies.

For me, it‘s the unhealthy foods that put a smile on my face - chocolate, cakes and ice cream - well, I do have a sweet tooth! It might seem obvious that food that’s bad for our waistline, usually makes us happy, at least in the short term. Most of us get this feeling when we use food as a quick pick-me-up. But dieticians tell us that eating bad food long term, not only makes us put on weight but can lead to other health conditions such as diabetes, and it can also affect our mental state and bring on depression.

The link between our mind and food has been looked at by scientists. They‘ve recently found that it’s the bacteria in our gut that affects our mood. It‘s thought we have 39 trillion of these simple, small organisms in our body. Researchers at McMaster University in Canada and University College Cork in Ireland, have found that certain ’good‘ bacteria help reduce anxiety in mice. And researchers at Kyushu University also found that germs help reduce stress and anxiety in mice. Experts believe that, for us humans, this means food with ’good‘ bacteria can improve the way we feel.

Many food products are claiming to be high in this ’good‘ bacteria and some of the best types are homemade fermented food like miso soup, yoghurt and sauerkraut. This really makes me think twice about what I eat — maybe I should change my diet to perk me up! Doctor Michael Mosley would agree. He’s been looking into this for the BBC and says the best food to cheer us up is in a “Mediterranean diet. Olive oil; oily fish, full of omega 3, which is really good for the brain; whole grains; lots of fruits and vegetables. Sugar: terrible for you!”

So maybe it‘s time to lay off the fatty and sugary things. Eating healthily may seem simple, even if the science behind it is complex. It’s not rocket science but this is further evidence for the saying ‘we are what we eat‘ — the person we are is determined by the food we eat. There are other factors that can change our mood but it seems we have some ability to improve how we feel by controlling what we put on our plate. Does your diet affect your mood?

vocabulary.entry: sweet tooth [n.] /ˌswiːt ˈtuːθ/ 爱吃甜食 (口语)
vocabulary.example: She has a sweet tooth and loves chocolate cake.
vocabulary.translation: 她爱吃甜食，喜欢巧克力蛋糕。

vocabulary.entry: pick-me-up [n.] /ˈpɪk miː ʌp/ 提神的东西；小零食 (口语)
vocabulary.example: A cup of coffee is a good pick-me-up in the afternoon.
vocabulary.translation: 下午一杯咖啡是很好的提神饮品。

vocabulary.entry: perk up [phr.] /pɜːk ʌp/ 使振作；使活跃
vocabulary.example: A short walk in the fresh air can perk you up.
vocabulary.translation: 在新鲜空气中短暂散步可以让你振作起来。

vocabulary.entry: lay off [phr.] /leɪ ɒf/ 停止；戒掉 (口语)
vocabulary.example: You should lay off sugary drinks if you want to lose weight.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你想减肥，就应该戒掉含糖饮料。

vocabulary.entry: feast on [phr.] /fiːst ɒn/ 尽情享受；大吃
vocabulary.example: The guests feasted on a delicious roast dinner.
vocabulary.translation: 客人们尽情享用了美味的烤晚餐。

vocabulary.entry: put on weight [phr.] /pʊt ɒn weɪt/ 体重增加；发胖
vocabulary.example: Eating too much junk food can make you put on weight.
vocabulary.translation: 吃太多垃圾食品会让你体重增加。

vocabulary.entry: bring on [phr.] /brɪŋ ɒn/ 导致；引起
vocabulary.example: Stress can bring on headaches.
vocabulary.translation: 压力会导致头痛。

vocabulary.entry: look into [phr.] /lʊk ˈɪntə/ 调查；研究
vocabulary.example: The police are looking into the cause of the accident.
vocabulary.translation: 警方正在调查事故原因。

vocabulary.entry: fermented food [n.] /fɜːˈmentɪd fuːd/ 发酵食品
vocabulary.example: Fermented foods like kimchi are rich in probiotics.
vocabulary.translation: 像泡菜这样的发酵食品富含益生菌。

vocabulary.entry: cheer up [phr.] /tʃɪər ʌp/ 使高兴；使振作
vocabulary.example: A funny movie can cheer me up when I‘m sad.
vocabulary.translation: 当我难过时，一部有趣的电影可以让我高兴起来。

vocabulary.entry: Mediterranean diet [n.] /ˌmedɪtəˈreɪniən ˈdaɪət/ 地中海饮食
vocabulary.example: The Mediterranean diet is rich in vegetables and olive oil.
vocabulary.translation: 地中海饮食富含蔬菜和橄榄油。

vocabulary.entry: omega 3 [n.] /ˈəʊmɪɡə θriː/ 欧米伽3脂肪酸
vocabulary.example: Salmon is a good source of omega 3.
vocabulary.translation: 三文鱼是欧米伽3的良好来源。

vocabulary.entry: whole grains [n. pl.] /həʊl ɡreɪnz/ 全谷物 (单数: whole grain)
vocabulary.example: Brown rice and oats are examples of whole grains.
vocabulary.translation: 糙米和燕麦是全谷物的例子。

vocabulary.entry: rocket science [n.] /ˈrɒkɪt ˈsaɪəns/ 高深的学问 (口语；比喻)
vocabulary.example: Cooking a good meal isn’t rocket science.
vocabulary.translation: 做一顿好饭不是什么高深的学问。

vocabulary.entry: be determined by [phr.] /biː dɪˈtɜːmɪnd baɪ/ 由……决定
vocabulary.example: Your success is determined by your hard work.
vocabulary.translation: 你的成功取决于你的努力。

vocabulary.entry: it’s no wonder [phr.] /ɪts nəʊ ˈwʌndə/ 难怪；不足为奇
vocabulary.example: It‘s no wonder you’re tired after that long walk.
vocabulary.translation: 走了那么长的路，难怪你累了。

vocabulary.term: put a smile on one‘s face [phr.]
vocabulary.entry: put a smile on one‘s face [phr.] /pʊt ə smaɪl ɒn wʌnz feɪs/ 使某人开心
vocabulary.example: Her kind words put a smile on my face.
vocabulary.translation: 她亲切的话语让我露出了笑容。

vocabulary.entry: in the short term [phr.] /ɪn ðə ʃɔːt tɜːm/ 在短期内
vocabulary.example: In the short term, this solution will save money.
vocabulary.translation: 在短期内，这个解决方案会省钱。

vocabulary.term: lay off the fatty and sugary things [phr.]
vocabulary.entry: lay off the fatty and sugary things [phr.] /leɪ ɒf ðə ˈfæti ənd ˈʃʊɡəri θɪŋz/ 少吃高脂肪和高糖的食物
vocabulary.example: The doctor told him to lay off the fatty and sugary things.
vocabulary.translation: 医生告诉他少吃高脂肪和高糖的食物。

vocabulary.entry: affect one‘s mood [phr.] /əˈfekt wʌnz muːd/ 影响某人的情绪
vocabulary.example: Lack of sleep can affect your mood.
vocabulary.translation: 睡眠不足会影响你的情绪。
